reason: Every number in it reproduces. Driving master.html?v=approach&state=owner-flight at 1440 after fonts.ready: .b-who, .b-when, .b-sub and .b-todayLabel all have box left 186 and ink left 186/187 (actualBoundingBoxLeft 0 to -1); .b-num ('79', Geist Mono 148px) has box left 186 and ink left 194 — an 8px indent on the largest object on the page, in a composition whose only structure is one column. At the 96px medium (phone) the same measurement gives 5px, as stated. Sweeping leading digits at 148px the ink offset is 5px for '4' and 7-8px for every other digit, so the countdown does shift the hero glyph as it ticks. The row claim holds too: .b-grab is a <button> with padding 0 8px whose border box starts at 734, the same as .b-title (ink 735) and .b-date (ink 734), so 'SHOWN' ink starts at 742 — three ragged left edges inside one item. A red guide dropped at x=186 and x=734 shows both in the rendered page, not just in the numbers. This is not taste and it is not already handled: there is no optical correction anywhere in b.css or shell.css (the only .num rule is tabular-nums in shell.css:122), and it restates no gate — audit.mjs checks palette, weights, families, contrast, targets, radii, motion, ramp and leading, none of which look at ink left edges. The fix is margin only, so it touches no locked constraint. At a 9.5 bar with Stripe and Linear named as benchmarks, optically aligning display numerals to the measure is table stakes.
sharpenedFix: Take the negative-margin option, not the family swap. In b.css add `margin-left: -0.05em` to .b-num (line 56) and to .b-ogNum (line 555): em resolves against each element's own font-size, so one declaration corrects 7.4px at 148px, 4.8px at 96px and 2.4px at 48px, matching the measured 8/5/2px offsets. .b-count is display:flex with gap 12px, so pulling the first flex item left moves '.b-unit' with it and the optical gap between '79' and 'DAYS' is preserved; .b-ogNum is a block in a flex column, so no side effect there. Do NOT take the finding's alternative of setting the count in Geist — .b-away and .b-ogNum are mono and the mono numeral is this direction's character; changing the family to buy 6px would cost more than it gains. Leave the residual per-digit drift (about 2.4px at 148px after correction) alone; it is intrinsic to the face and chasing it per digit is over-engineering. For the row control, do NOT use `padding: 0` plus a `::before { inset: -6px -8px }` overlay as written — .b-grab:hover paints `background: var(--fore-06)`, and with zero padding that ground hugs the letters and reads as a defect. Instead keep `padding: 0 8px` and add `margin-left: -8px` to .b-grab (b.css:364). The text then starts at 734, flush with .b-title and .b-date; the 28x56 hit box and the hover pill's breathing room are untouched, so audit.mjs's target check needs no pseudo-element to satisfy it; and there is room to bleed into — .b-item sits at left:124px with .b-tick at left:-27px (96px/-23px at the phone medium), leaving over 12px of clearance at both mediums.
